target_customer: Voters (free); funded by donations and grants as a nonprofit
problem: Registering to vote, checking registration and absentee or long distance voting were confusing and fragmented.
business_model: Nonprofit funded by grants and donations

founders.name: Debra Cleaver
founders.background_notes: Removed by the board in 2019; sued in 2022 alleging wrongful termination (outcome not found)

competitors.name: Rock the Vote
competitors.what: Online voter registration tool, among the first

technical_complexity.rationale: Web forms and state rules; scale peaks around elections.

defensibility.rationale: Trusted exact-name brand, but others offered similar tools.

market_need_then: Low turnout and registration friction in the 2016 election; YC reports 1.5 million helped to register on a $366k budget.

branding.name_origin: Renamed from Long Distance Voter in April 2016 after the group outgrew the old name.
branding.domain_note: Vote.org domain; how it was obtained was not found.

rebrands.why: The group had outgrown the original name and relaunched with YC funding.

branding.community_and_virality: Rebranding agency case study and press (Bustle) cover the relaunch.

brand_strength.rationale: Exact-match descriptive domain and strong press during 2016; the name directly states the mission.

outcome_analysis: Vote.org began in 2008 as Long Distance Voter and relaunched under the new name in April 2016 as a YC nonprofit, reporting 1.5 million people helped to register on a small budget. The group persists, but founder Cleaver was removed by the board in 2019 and sued in 2022, with reported loss of promised funding. This is a nonprofit, so startup outcome factors apply loosely.
notes: Competitors are from 2012 coverage because no 2016 comparison was found; HelloVote (September 2016) appeared later. Amount of YC support not found. Sources disagree on the date of Cleaver's removal. Reported lost $4M Sage Weil pledge is from a Wikipedia mirror.
